strategies.desc: Direct translation of the reference: 8 sequential all_reduce calls, each preceded by forward bidiagonal coupling and followed by backward uncoupling. 8 all_reduce dispatches total. Represents the naive approach with maximum dispatch overhead but simplest correctness verification.

strategies.name: Fused Local Ops Single Buffer
strategies.desc: Merge all forward coupling and backward uncoupling loops into single-pass kernels per stage, reusing one buffer in-place. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but reduces memory allocation overhead and local compute fragmentation. Trades code complexity for fewer intermediate tensor allocations.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + AllGather Chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all_reduce with a reduce_scatter (producing W shards) followed by all_gather on rank-local shard after local coupling/uncoupling. 16 dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller per-dispatch payload (1/W of all_reduce size for reduce_scatter phase). Better bandwidth utilization when network is the bottleneck.

strategies.name: Pipelined AllReduce with Overlapping Computation
strategies.desc: Launch all_reduce asynchronously where possible, interleaving backward uncoupling of stage i with forward coupling and all_reduce of stage i+1. Requires careful dependency tracking via xm barriers. 8 dispatches but overlaps communication with local compute, reducing wall-clock time.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level AllReduce
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node structure (if num_nodes > 1): perform intra-node all_reduce, apply coupling/uncoupling once per node, then inter-node all_reduce, then broadcast back. Reduces cross-node traffic by factor of cores_per_node. Fewer large dispatches for inter-node, more small dispatches for intra-node (approximately 8*3 = 24 dispatches assuming two levels).
